pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three rows are 0 and CHECK rejects 2; migration 0002 sets NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.
'AC-2' test asserts exact list with ★ only on the starred item.
'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1, asserts only those, in id order.
'AC-4' test covers / and /?show=all with exact order.

The final commit 85fd5a1 ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. No test now names AC-5, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'. The behaviour is implemented, but the item is unmet by the rule.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__.
'AC-7' test imports traffic/routes.json and asserts it contains /?show=starred.

findings.what: Commit 85fd5a1 ('Follow-up edits', a bot commit) removed the 'AC-5:' prefix from the link test title. No test names AC-5 now, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'. The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and doesn't mention this edit.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'.

findings.what: The PR says it still refuses spaces and '#', which is true. But the commit adds a '/?q=a b' failure case that passes only because of the space, and the error message still says 'paths starting with "/"' without mentioning that queries are allowed.

lenses.note: Change matches the spec's intent; the traffic-check relaxation is needed for AC-7.
Every state-table row has a test. AC-5 is unnamed after the last commit.
Tests assert behaviour. I did not run them (the workers runtime may be unavailable here); CI runs them. The AC-5 title was stripped in the last commit.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is safe. The SQL is static.
Query input is checked against an allowlist, titles are HTML-escaped, and there are no injection paths.
The page has only minimal plain HTML, with no styling or UI files in the diff.
No UI components or flows beyond two links; no browser available.
'Changed after the go: nothing' is accurate for the spec, but the late commit weakened a test's AC naming without mention.
